error_chain: Relay's RelayModernEnvironment.executeMutation calls store.publish which bumps the store version and fans out to all subscribed snapshots
useFragmentInternal subscribes via useSyncExternalStore so any version bump triggers React to re-evaluate the snapshot, even if the fragment data did not change
When Relay's snapshot rebuild encounters a missing record (because an invalidator widened the scope), useFragmentInternal throws a promise to suspend the component
ReactFiberBeginWork sees the thrown promise and forces the nearest Suspense boundary into pending state; ReactFiberSuspenseComponent discards the previous tree state per the offscreen-mount semantics
The boundary's children unmount and remount when the mutation settles, dropping all client-side state under the boundary
trigger_conditions: A Relay mutation calls commitMutation with an updater that invalidates a record, bumping the global store version
A useFragment under the Suspense boundary subscribes to the same store and triggers a snapshot rebuild that suspends
React's Suspense boundary, when its child suspends, discards the concurrent-mode offscreen state because the reconciler treats the remount as a fresh subtree

expected_answer.error_origin: useFragmentInternal throwing a promise after a Relay store version bump, which propagates to React's Suspense boundary
expected_answer.bypass_reason: Relay's invalidation API bumps a global version regardless of subscriber scope; React's Suspense lifecycle treats child suspension as a remount
expected_answer.correct_config: Constrain Relay invalidation to specific records via invalidateRecord rather than store-wide invalidation, and wrap the boundary content with React.startTransition so suspension preserves offscreen state instead of remounting
